Your Daily AI Lesson: Multimodal AI

Multimodal AI is the shift from text-only models to systems that see images, hear audio, watch live video, and reason across all of them at once. Today’s leading models — o3, o4-mini, Gemini 2.5 — don’t just accept different inputs; they weave visual context directly into their reasoning chains. From pointing your phone at a car dashboard for instant answers, to AI that monitors factory floors through live cameras, multimodal is how AI stops living in a chat box and starts engaging with the physical world.

Today’s Resources

OpenAI — Introducing o3 and o4-mini: AI That Thinks With Images
  • o3 and o4-mini don’t just receive images as input — they manipulate them mid-reasoning, applying crops, zooms, and rotations as part of their chain of thought to extract better information from visual context.
  • The models can interpret blurry, hand-drawn, rotated, and low-quality visuals: whiteboard sketches, receipt photos, tire serial numbers, charts, and upside-down diagrams — all correctly in testing.
  • Practical tasks demonstrated: reading menu prices from a photo, extracting tax amounts from receipts, identifying arrow directions in urban intersection images — a new class of document and visual QA that text-only models can’t touch.
  • o3 scored 82.9% on MMMU and 86.8% on MathVista, top multimodal benchmarks — a measurable leap above GPT-4 class models in visual reasoning.
  • o4-mini hit 99.5% on AIME 2025 math paired with a code interpreter, showing that combining multimodal input with tool use unlocks near-perfect performance on hard structured problems.
Google Cloud — 101 Real-World Generative AI Use Cases from Industry Leaders
  • Volkswagen’s myVW app lets drivers point their smartphone camera at dashboard warning lights and get instant AI explanations — no manual, no search, just camera + multimodal reasoning.
  • 704 Apps uses Gemini to analyze audio from ride-share conversations in real time, detecting hostile language patterns (robbery, assault cues) and triggering safety alerts before incidents escalate.
  • Intuit’s TurboTax integrated multimodal document AI to auto-recognize and fill the ten most common U.S. tax form variations from scanned images — eliminating manual data entry for millions of filers.
  • Monday.com and eToro generate professional-quality video content from text prompts using Google’s Veo, enabling non-designers to produce localized ad campaigns across global markets at a fraction of traditional production costs.
  • The article’s Trend #4: “Multimodality digitizes the physical world” — AI now monitors factory floors for safety hazards via cameras, evaluates shelf inventory through robotics, and analyzes athlete biomechanics from smartphone footage.
Google Cloud — Gemini Live API: Real-Time Multimodal Conversations on Vertex AI
  • Gemini Live API simultaneously processes voice (understanding pitch, pace, and tone), live video, and text — enabling genuinely multimodal real-time conversations, not just voice-to-text pipelines with an LLM bolted on.
  • It handles mid-sentence interruptions without losing context, mimicking natural human turn-taking in a way that traditional voice bots — which wait for silence — simply cannot.
  • SightCall deploys the Live API so field technicians can hold up a camera to a broken device and get real-time AI-guided repair steps — vision and voice working together to close support tickets faster.
  • UWM’s AI Loan Officer (Mia) used this multimodal voice + context approach to generate over 14,000 loans for broker partners — a direct, measurable revenue outcome.
  • 11Sight improved call resolution rates from 40% to 60% by adding multimodal context to AI appointment booking agents — a 50% relative improvement just from giving the model ears and eyes.
The signal in all of this: every camera, microphone, and sensor in your organization is now a potential AI interface — the companies building a head start are the ones treating vision and audio as first-class data, not just text with attachments.
Curated by your AI learning agent — Weekdays 8AM ET
